summary: Describes how an AAA server such as RADIUS or Diameter can help a Mobile IPv4 node and its home agent set up the strong authentication they need, using the security association the node already shares with its home AAA server.

eli5.summary: A traveling phone and its home base need a secret password. Instead of setting one up by hand, they borrow one from the login system the phone already uses.

questions: how does mobile ipv4 get keys from aaa
what is a key generation nonce
what is a mobility security association
subtitle: Letting a roaming Mobile IPv4 device derive fresh registration keys from the login credentials it already shares with its home AAA server.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv4 needs strong authentication between a mobile node and its home agent, but a roaming node may have no security association with its home agent or the foreign agent it is visiting.
tldr.mechanism: The node asks for key material in new registration extensions. The AAA server returns a random Key Generation Nonce, and the node computes the key as HMAC-SHA1 over the nonce and its identifier, using the secret it already shares with the AAA server.
tldr.outcome: The node ends up with derived Mobility Security Associations with its home agent and/or foreign agent, with no more security than the existing AAA association provides.

today: RFC 3957 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 3344, the Mobile IPv4 specification it extends.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem
sections.content:
AAA servers (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting), such as RADIUS and Diameter, are used to authenticate and authorize dial-up computers. Mobile IP for IPv4 requires strong authentication between the mobile node and its home agent. When the mobile node already shares an AAA Security Association with its home AAA server, that association can be used to create derived Mobility Security Associations between the mobile node and its home agent, and between the node and the foreign agent that currently offers connectivity.

The RFC specifies extensions to Mobile IP registration messages that do this. It assumes the AAA entities have their own means, outside this document, of exchanging keys.
sections.eli5: A phone already has a login with its home network. This RFC lets that login help the phone make new secret handshakes with the helpers it meets while traveling.

sections.title: Key Terms
sections.content:
A Mobility Security Association is a simplex connection that authenticates Mobile IPv4 control traffic between a mobile node and home agent, or mobile node and foreign agent. It is identified by the two endpoint addresses and an SPI (a 32-bit Security Parameters Index). Two nodes typically need only one.

A registration key is a key used in such an association; it is typically used only once or a very few times, to verify a small volume of authentication data. A Key Generation Nonce is nonce data used to create a key. The AAA key, called AAA-key, is the secret in the AAA Security Association, which may be based on the node's IP address or its Network Access Identifier (NAI).

The mobile node can be identified by its NAI without having a home address at all, which is why a node may need keys before it has set up a home agent relationship.
sections.eli5: A security association is a private handshake between two parties. A nonce is a one-time random number mixed into the recipe so each handshake key is new.

sections.title: How the Exchange Works
sections.content:
The mobile node adds request extensions to its Registration Request:

  • If it has no association with the foreign agent, it SHOULD include an MN-FA Key Generation Nonce Request.
  • If it has none with the home agent, it MUST include an MN-HA Key Generation Nonce Request.
  • If it added either, it MUST add the MN-AAA Authentication extension.

The foreign agent passes the request into the AAA infrastructure. After the home AAA server verifies the authentication, it generates the key material and distributes the keys to the home and foreign agents through the AAA protocol. Those parts are out of scope here; only the Registration Request and Reply with the extensions are specified. The AAA server MAY also send unsolicited key material, and the node MUST then calculate new keys.

On the reply, if a MN-HA nonce was requested, the node MUST create or update its home agent association from the returned material, and MUST discard the reply if no MN-HA reply extension is present. It then checks the Mobile-Home Authentication extension; if that fails it discards the reply and the new association and reverts to the old one. A reply with a MN-FA nonce likewise leads to a foreign agent association checked via the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension. Any reply carrying a nonce extension MUST also carry the matching authentication extension made with the new key.
sections.eli5: The traveler says, "I need new secret codes," through the local helper. The home login office makes a random number, and the traveler uses it with their private password to cook up the same code the helpers received.

sections.title: Deriving the Key
sections.content:
The AAA home server identifies the mobile node by the NAI if present in the Registration Request, otherwise by the Home Address. It generates a random value of at least 128 bits as the Key Generation Nonce and puts it in the Key Generation Nonce Reply extension.

The mobile node then computes key = HMAC-SHA1 (AAA-key, {Key Generation Nonce || mobile node identifier}), where || is concatenation, and builds the Mobility Security Association from the result. All nodes implementing these extensions MUST implement HMAC-SHA1; other message authentication codes or keyed hash functions MAY be used. The algorithm is configured in the AAA Security Association, indexed by the AAA SPI.

Home agent associations also need a replay protection method. The supported replay methods are 2 (timestamps) and 3 (nonces), as defined in RFC 3344; 0 and 1 are reserved.
sections.eli5: Both the traveler and the home office know a secret password. They mix it with the same random number and name, so both end up with the same new key without ever sending the key itself.

sections.title: The Four Extensions
sections.content:
Four new registration extensions are defined, each a generalized extension with a Subtype so other key sources can be added later. This document defines subtype 1 (from AAA) for each.

  • MN-FA Key Generation Nonce Request (type 40): carries the Mobile Node SPI the node will assign. The subtype 1 data is zero length and MUST appear before the MN-AAA Authentication extension.
  • MN-FA Key Generation Nonce Reply (type 41): subtype 1 data holds Lifetime in seconds, AAA SPI, FA SPI, an Algorithm Identifier and the Key Generation Nonce of at least 128 bits. It MUST appear before the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension.
  • MN-HA Key Generation Nonce Request (type 42): like the FA request, for the home agent.
  • MN-HA Key Generation Nonce Reply (type 43): has Lifetime, and subtype 1 data of AAA SPI, HA SPI, Algorithm Identifier, Replay Method and the nonce. It MUST appear before the MN-HA Authentication extension.

All four types are non-skippable. If the foreign agent has no association with the node and sees no MN-FA reply extension, it MAY change the reply Code to MISSING_MN_FA (value 107), failing the registration.
sections.eli5: There are four kinds of note: ask the local helper for a code, get the local helper's code ingredients, and the same two for the home base.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The derived associations offer no higher level of security than the underlying AAA Security Association. To deny an adversary unbounded time to break it, that AAA association MUST be refreshed periodically, though provisioning and refresh of the AAA key are outside the scope of this document.

The reply extensions carry only nonces, which are used to derive keys, so they expose nothing that could help recover the key shared between the mobile node and the AAA server. The authors do not believe the specification introduces any new vulnerability.

Appendix A lists requirements for the AAA key distribution mechanism, including strong and fresh session keys, replay detection, authenticated parties, no reliance on plaintext passwords, and no exposure of keys beyond the AAAH and the FA or HA.
sections.eli5: The random numbers sent around are harmless alone, but the old password still guards everything, so it has to be changed every so often.

data.title: Generalized MN-FA Key Generation Nonce Request

fields.name: Subtype
fields.desc: Says how the subtype data is used to generate the registration key.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Bytes of subtype data plus 4 for the Mobile Node SPI.

fields.name: Mobile Node SPI
fields.desc: SPI the node assigns for the new Mobility Security Association.

items.label: MN-FA-KeyGen Request
items.desc: Node asks for foreign agent key material.

items.label: MN-FA-KeyGen Reply
items.desc: Returns the nonce and SPIs for the foreign agent.

items.label: MN-HA-KeyGen Request
items.desc: Node asks for home agent key material.

items.label: MN-HA-KeyGen Reply
items.desc: Returns the nonce, SPIs and replay method for the home agent.
